name: Uma Baker

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. This is confidential. What is a normal workday for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and lead eight people who handle staff complaints at a large retail company. We take statements, check shift records and write a report when someone says a manager treated them unfairly. I have a bachelor’s degree and have done this for nine years; I’m solid at it, though our senior investigator handles the hardest cases. I like getting a worker’s lost hours corrected. I hate hearing that a form closed a complaint before anyone spoke to the worker.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: Who is at home, and how much room would you have if your work changed?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My husband, Ravi, is a payroll accountant at another large company, and our children are ten and fourteen. We have a mortgage and about a year of expenses saved; my pay is high for this management role. There are plenty of similar offices nearby. I’ve never used an AI tool, and I’m active with our staff union because a worker needs a person to challenge a bad decision.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the team to keep hearing each worker before closing a complaint. A small tool may sort dates, but it cannot replace an account of what happened on a shift.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My role and Ravi’s payroll job should carry on much as before. Our year of savings and two paychecks make the mortgage feel secure, though I still watch whether complaints get rushed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I’d keep our weekly case meeting and require a worker call before any complaint is closed. During the first year Ravi and I would continue paying an extra 250 monthly toward the mortgage while both wages hold and our year of savings stays intact.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about our household. I would still be cross if the company used a small time saving to close cases without a conversation.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What case stays in your mind?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A shelf worker lost two evening shifts because a supervisor entered the wrong code. The shelf worker’s missing wages were fixed only after we asked what happened.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why keep a year saved while overpaying the mortgage?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The reserve is for a real job loss or illness. I would stop the extra payment before I used it for ordinary bills.

say: I’d keep hearing **each worker** before closing a complaint about a shift.
A small date sorter cannot replace a **full shift account** from the person involved.
think: Both **office incomes** should carry on, keeping the household pay steady.
Our **one-year reserve** and two wages make the mortgage feel secure.
do: Keep **weekly case meetings** and call workers before closure.
Pay **250 extra monthly** on the mortgage only while wages and the year reserve hold.
feel: I feel **calm** about work and household money.
S0.quote: The shelf worker’s missing wages were fixed only after we asked what happened.
fieldNote: She insists on **worker testimony** before closing a case.
High pay and **a year saved** make the household secure here.
Mortgage overpayments stop before the **reserve** is used.

steps.text: Keep weekly complaint reviews and call workers before closing each case
Pay 250 extra monthly on mortgage only while both wages and one-year reserve hold

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AI will draft case reports and check shift data, so workers must see how often it gets a complaint wrong. I’d ask the union to inspect rejected cases before staff posts are removed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A smaller team could mean the company combines two complaint desks and cuts one manager. Ravi’s payroll checking is exposed too, so the household could lose hours on both sides even with a year saved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I’d ask the union steward to pick thirty closed complaints for a joint error review with my senior investigator. In the first year I’d seek a written agreement that no case closes without a worker’s chance to speak, and I’d suspend the 250 mortgage overpayment if either household wage falls.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious about both jobs, though we can live on the reserve for a while. I do not want workers to discover the new rule only when they appeal.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you use the new tool yourself?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not until someone shows me the errors on real cases. I’ve never used AI and would rather work with my investigator on the paper record first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the union agreement actually say?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A worker gets a named contact and a chance to challenge the account before closure. The union would check the count of reversals each month.

say: I’d demand **wrong-case counts** before team cuts.
Workers need a **chance to speak** before any closure.
think: My **manager post** could go if two desks combine.
Ravi’s payroll work could also lose **hours**.
A year saved buys **time**, not replacement wages for both jobs.
do: Ask the **union steward and investigator** to review thirty closed cases for AI errors.
Seek a **written worker appeal rule** and pause mortgage overpayments if either wage falls.
feel: I feel **anxious** about both household jobs.
S1.quote: A worker gets a named contact and a chance to challenge the account before closure.
fieldNote: She delegates tool review to **trusted people** before any personal use.
She sees **two desk incomes** exposed in steady disruption.
The overpayment pauses when **either wage** falls.

steps.text: Ask union steward and investigator to review thirty closed complaints for AI errors
Seek a written union rule for worker contact and appeal before closure

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask for written notice and a worker appeal route before the company gives complaints to AGI. I’d also ask the union to press for paid transition time, not a farewell speech.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2028 could take my interviewing notes, shift checks and judgments, so I expect my post to go. Ravi’s payroll work is thinking work too and could go at the same time; a year saved will not replace two salaries forever.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Tonight Ravi and I would stop the planned kitchen extension and keep its deposit liquid. Before 2028 I’d help the union demand a written severance and paid-transition agreement, and I’d ask our mortgage lender which documents a job-loss plan needs; in the first year after AGI, if both jobs end I’d submit applications for public income support while we search nearby postings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m alarmed. A year of savings keeps me from panicking, but the idea of two wage letters arriving together would keep me awake.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move to another complaints office?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I might apply for a short paid bridge if one is posted, but those offices use thinking work too. Another complaints office would still face 2028 AGI, even if its logo were different.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say to your children about the extension?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We would explain that the house is sound and the cash may have to pay its mortgage. I would not ask them to carry our job worries.

say: I’d seek **written notice** and worker appeals before AGI rollout.
The union should press for **paid transition time**.
think: I **expect my complaints post** to end in 2028.
Ravi’s payroll job **could face** the same thinking deadline.
A year saved cannot replace **two salaries** indefinitely.
do: Stop the **kitchen extension** and keep its deposit liquid.
Demand **severance and paid transition** through the union; apply for income support if both wages end.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about losing two incomes.
S2.quote: Another complaints office would still face 2028 AGI, even if its logo were different.
fieldNote: The **2028 thinking deadline** threatens both household jobs.
She treats nearby office posts as **temporary bridges**, not shelter.
Public support is an **application after loss**, not assumed income.

steps.text: Stop the kitchen extension and keep its deposit available for mortgage bills
Help the union demand written severance and paid transition time before 2028
Submit public income-support applications after 2028 only if both jobs end

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say five years gives the company time to negotiate job sharing and real severance instead of cutting a desk overnight. The union should see the case numbers and staffing dates every year.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ravi and I could save more while both wages arrive, but 2031 AGI could still take both our kinds of office work. I am not eager to train for another desk post that can be automated on the same date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Beginning January 2027 we’d move an extra 200 monthly to savings while both wages hold and keep the mortgage current. I’d ask the union to propose a paid job-share plan for remaining human complaint reviews, then in the first year after 2031 take reduced hours only if the written pay plus Ravi’s income covers our mortgage and school costs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious, but five years means we can negotiate before anyone’s wage falls. I would rather share paid work than watch a colleague leave with nothing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if Ravi’s payroll job also goes?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then the job-share plan is not enough for us, and I would use the reserve while searching posted work. We would apply for public income support if eligible rather than pretend one reduced wage covers everything.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you give up in a job share?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Hours and some pay, but not the right to hear a worker before closing a complaint. I would want the split and wage in writing.

say: I’d seek **paid job sharing** before desk cuts.
The union should review **case counts** and staffing dates yearly.
think: Ravi and I could **save more** while both wages arrive before 2031.
I would avoid another desk post with **the same AGI exposure** in 2031.
do: Save **200 extra monthly** only while both wages and mortgage payments hold.
Propose a **written job share** and take reduced hours only if household pay covers mortgage and school costs.
feel: I feel **anxious** but have time to negotiate.
S3.quote: I would rather share paid work than watch a colleague leave with nothing.
fieldNote: She prefers **shared paid hours** to an abrupt cut.
The job share fails if **Ravi’s wage** also disappears.
The plan needs **written pay** covering mortgage and school costs.

steps.text: Transfer an extra 200 monthly to savings while both wages and mortgage payments hold
Ask union to propose a paid job-share plan for human complaint reviews

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say a decade lets employers and workers write down the terms before the complaint desk changes. I’d ask for paid retraining and a real appeal route, not a promise that nobody will be hurt.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 53 in 2036 and both children would be grown. If both wages hold, we could reduce the mortgage and keep our year reserve; but my case decisions and Ravi’s payroll still face 2036 AGI, so two salaries are not guaranteed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In January 2027 Ravi and I would continue the 250 mortgage overpayment only while both wages hold and our year reserve remains intact. I’d ask the union for an annual written review of staffing, case appeals and paid training offers; in the first year after 2036 I’d apply for public income support if both posts close and use the reserve for a search rather than buy another desk job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy, with a decade to put the house on firmer ground. I would still want the union agreement written before my last working day.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you leave now for another company?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. A different complaints team could pay for a while, but its thinking work faces 2036 AI as well.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your children in ten years?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say we used the good earning years to keep the house affordable. I would not tell them that steady work was guaranteed forever.

say: I’d seek **written change terms** before the complaint desk shrinks.
Workers need **paid retraining and appeals** while their jobs change.
think: If both wages hold, we could reduce **the mortgage** and keep our one-year reserve.
My case decisions and Ravi’s payroll still face **2036 AGI**, so two salaries are uncertain.
do: Overpay the **mortgage by 250** only while both wages and the year reserve hold.
Ask for **annual union reviews** and apply for income support after 2036 if both posts close.
feel: I feel **uneasy** but have time to make the mortgage more affordable.
S4.quote: A different complaints team could pay for a while, but its thinking work faces 2036 AI as well.
fieldNote: She rejects another desk as a **permanent escape**.
She plans **income-support applications** after both jobs close, without assuming payment.

steps.text: Overpay mortgage by 250 monthly only while both wages and one-year reserve hold
Ask union for annual written reviews of staffing appeals and paid training offers
Apply for public income support after 2036 only if both desk jobs close

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because both my case team and Ravi’s payroll work could end together. A written severance figure, paid transition time and a real worker appeal route would help. Our savings give us a year to search, not two new salaries.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask what a worker does when a complaint is closed by a system before anyone listens. A closed case can still leave a person short of rent.

headlineQuote: A closed case can still leave a person short of rent.
portrait: **Uma**, 43, is an experienced staff-complaints manager with a bachelor’s degree.
High pay and **one year saved** support a mortgage and two school-age children.
She has **never used AI** and asks the union for human review before case closure.
She prepares for **two exposed desk incomes** through savings and written worker agreements.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove both her complaint role and Ravi’s payroll job.
whatWouldHelp: **Written severance**, paid transition time and a real worker appeal route would help.
